title: Calling APIs from Kotlin
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of calling apis from kotlin using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates calling apis from kotlin.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Calling APIs from Kotlin** as part of **Serialization, Networking, and Application Integration**. Integration code must validate external data, handle timeouts and failure states, keep credentials outside source control, and test boundary behavior. Use the subtopics—HTTP Client Libraries, Parsing API Responses, Timeouts, Retries, and Error Handling—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.text: Calling APIs from Kotlin removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
